blocks.text: The two-day crossing of the Drake Passage continues. The ship crosses the Antarctic Convergence, where cold northward-flowing waters meet warmer subantarctic waters. The marine life and seabird species change along the way. You’ll watch from the ship, and wildlife sightings depend on natural conditions.
A white twin-hulled yacht and a yellow inflatable boat by a rocky shore
A yacht on blue water beside a small inflatable boat

The Antarctic leg begins as the ship passes the snow-covered Melchior Islands and sails through Schollaert Channel, between Brabant and Anvers islands. Around you are snowy peaks, blue and white ice, and Antarctic wildlife. The expedition team decides the exact schedule for sailings and landings during this part of the trip.

On Danco Island, you may see gentoo penguins. Weddell and crabeater seals are also found nearby. At Neko Harbour, there may be a Zodiac cruise and a landing with views of glaciers and mountain peaks. In Paradise Bay, a Zodiac outing may offer a chance to see humpback and minke whales. After sailing through the Neumayer Channel, you may visit Port Lockroy on Goudier Island, where the former British research station now houses a museum and post office. Near Jougla Point, you may see gentoo penguins and blue-eyed shags. These are possible stops on days 4–7. Whether a landing takes place and on which day depends on conditions.
